title: Audit host-dispatched Engram writes for lost-reply handling: keep original identity, tell unsent from dispatched-without-reply, disclose and read back before any retry
outcome: Audit host-dispatched Engram writes for lost-reply handling: keep original identity, tell unsent from dispatched-without-reply, disclose and read back before any retry
acceptance: An inventory lists every TermAl host path that dispatches an Engram write (control operations over the adapter, and any host-issued CLI or MCP write), with file and function, and for each states how a lost or invalid reply is handled today.

For every write path in the inventory, the original dispatch identity and arguments (session, idempotency key, intent) are retained before send, and a lost reply is classified as either proven-unsent or dispatched-without-valid-reply; timeout or cancel alone is never treated as rollback.

A dispatched-without-valid-reply outcome is disclosed explicitly as unresolved to the caller or user. No mutation is retried automatically except as an identical replay through a path the code supports, with the exact retained originating session, idempotency key and intent, never with a newly built identity or time; an append-style operation is never repeated merely because its reply was lost. Any other retry of a mutation is preceded by a readback through Engram's supported contract, and a restored completed gate is read back with `show REF --notes --gates` before any repeat.

Each path changed by this work has a test that loses the reply after dispatch and shows the classification, the disclosure and the readback-before-retry, or identical replay, behaviour; paths already conforming are named with the existing test that shows it.
